The landing was rough — it always is — and the lost city of Zal swallowed them whole: heat, noise, green. the scholar Dr. Elena Vance grinned. 'Just like old times.' Alex Quinn grinned back. Old times had nearly killed them twice.

They made camp under strange stars. an ancient map pulsed on Alex Quinn's chest. Somewhere out there, the warlord's men was moving. The race, Alex Quinn thought, was already on. never leave a friend behind — time to prove it.

By dawn they were over the lost city of Zal, the green unrolling below like a held breath. Alex Quinn checked an ancient map one more time. It hummed faintly, the way true things do when they're near their home.

chapters.title: Into the Green
chapters.text:
Three days into the lost city of Zal, the trail went cold — and then hot: fresh boot prints, the warlord's men's mark, heading the same way. 'They're a day ahead,' the scholar Dr. Elena Vance said, 'but they're heavy. We're fast.'

The legend nearly ended it: rapids, a broken rope, Alex Quinn in the water with an ancient map in a waterproof bag and the scholar Dr. Elena Vance's hand the only solid thing in the world. 'Never leave a friend behind,' the scholar Dr. Elena Vance gasped. 'Your rule.'

At dawn the markers led to the ruins: stone teeth in the jungle's jaw. Alex Quinn stood at the gate with an ancient map humming louder. 'Whatever happens,' Alex Quinn said, 'we go together.'

chapters.title: The Ruins
chapters.text:
Alex Quinn took it and ran, because Alex Quinn is not an idiot. The chase through the collapsing ruins was the kind of thing they'd tell for years: swinging, sliding, the scholar Dr. Elena Vance with the rope, an ancient map in the bag, the whole place coming down.

the warlord's men's team hit them in the treasure chamber — of course it was the treasure chamber — and the standoff was pure cinema: an ancient map on its pedestal, two crews, one exit. 'Take it,' the warlord's men said, 'and die rich.'

The ruins of the lost city of Zal were a puzzle built by people who didn't want visitors. an ancient map was the key — literally; it fit a slot in the great door, and the stone sighed open after a thousand years.

chapters.title: The Price of Gold
chapters.text:
the warlord's men, bound and furious, offered everything: money, power, a share. Alex Quinn listened politely and said no politely, which infuriated the warlord's men more than any insult. Some people can't be bought. Some treasures can't be sold.

The trek out was worse than the trek in: the warlord's men's backup team, the river rising, the scholar Dr. Elena Vance feverish from a scratch that turned ugly. Alex Quinn carried the scholar Dr. Elena Vance and an ancient map in turns, and learned what shoulders are for.

At the rapids, they made their stand: outnumbered, outgunned, but holding the high ground and the moral ground, which as the scholar Dr. Elena Vance said weakly, 'is worth at least two guns.'

chapters.title: The Real Treasure
chapters.text:
The museum opening was black tie. Alex Quinn wore boots. the scholar Dr. Elena Vance, recovered and insufferable, wore a grin. an ancient map sat behind glass, humming faintly, home at last among people who'd care for it.

They stood before an ancient map one last time. It had started all this: the legend, the race, the ruin, the rescue. Alex Quinn saluted it. Some doors, once opened, stay open forever.

the warlord's men got fifteen years and a memoir deal. Alex Quinn got the kid's wide eyes and the scholar Dr. Elena Vance's friendship and a new map already arriving by courier. No return address. Of course.
